items.root_cause: Two mechanisms compound. (1) The Walmart builder's quantity fallback publishes a row whose printed quantity contradicts the store's unit-price attribute, when its own doctrine for the shape question is to refuse a row that cannot be reproduced; Walmart's attribute is a known-wrong source, so 176 distinct rows since 08-22 carry a size the name denies. (2) The union has no same-product supersession: the depth rule admits any older in-window capture that knows more products, and the ranker then takes the cheapest per-unit even when a NEWER capture of the same store carries the SAME product at a different price (18 live cells, 7 crowns) or its full-name twin (132 truncated July batch names, 3 live cells). A stale price therefore survives exactly as long as the 90-day window, and the July batch (no item_id, 60-char names) can be refreshed by nothing.

root_fix.what: (a) build-walmart-deals.ps1: when Get-NameQtyCandidates returns a quantity in the priced unit, none reproduces Walmart's unit price, and the derived/name ratio is not explained by a pack count parsed from the name, REFUSE the row (qty_basis 'REFUSED: name quantity disagrees with unit price, no pack count'), never publish it. (b) capture-depth-lib.ps1 Select-FreshestCaptureRows: same-store same-product supersession - when two in-window captures carry the same product (same item_id, else same exact name, else a 60-char name that is a prefix of the other), only the NEWEST capture's row is eligible; the depth rule then runs over the surviving rows exactly as today. ONE implementation (the lib), both callers (compare-deals enforces, audit-capture-eviction audits) follow.

items.deviation:
THREE deviations, all measured.
(1) ORDERING. The plan puts Remove-SupersededRows at the TOP of Select-FreshestCaptureRows. Simulated over candidates-2026-09-02, that ordering thins the older captures BEFORE the depth count and so lets a thinner newer capture evict a deeper older one - the 2026-08-06 class the item's own do_not_touch forbids. It moved 10 cells nobody had measured, every one dearer and every one a whole-capture eviction rather than a stale twin: clam-chowder Walmart 0.132->0.2445, facial-tissues 0.0069->0.0103, marshmallows 0.0731->0.105, dried-dill 1.5145->2.96, frosting 0.1099->0.1112, corn-muffin-mix 0.0847->0.0906, tomatillos 2.86->3.68, diapers Sam's 0.1402->0.18, stuffing-mix Sam's 0.2706->0.3325, tomato-paste Sam's 0.1108->0.1178. SHIPPED INSTEAD: the depth rule runs first on the untouched row set and supersession runs over the rows it kept, so a row is dropped only when the SAME product's newer row is itself eligible. 16 cells move, 0 unmeasured extras, no cell can lose its store.
(2) IDENTITY. The first cut preferred prod_key and fell back to the name; that split the exact pair the rule exists for, because the July batch rows carry no item_id while their full-name twins do ('id:54258473' vs 'nm:Great Value Gluten-Free Vegetable Broth, 32 oz Carton, Shelf'). The rebuild moved every exact-name twin and left vegetable-broth pricing from 2026-07-18. Identity is now the transitive UNION of same-id and same-name (with the 60-char unique-prefix widening); the second rebuild moved vegetable-broth 0.0399 -> 0.0469, the plan's predicted value.
(3) CELL VALUES. 8 of the plan's 22 cell_effects predicted the same product's newer price rather than the re-ranked cell. Measured on the rebuilt board: bar-soap Sam's 0.4988 -> 0.549 (Irish Spring, not Caress 0.6862), apples Sam's 1.44 -> 1.555 (Envy, not Wild Twist 1.6925), cherries Sam's 2.94 -> 3.74 (correct, but only after a second ruling - see below), blueberries Walmart 0.3178 -> 0.325 (not 0.4244), curry-powder Walmart 0.89 -> 0.9144 (not 1.06; Frontier and 27 Peaks are known-wrong). Four predicted moves do NOT happen because the newer twin's capture is not eligible under the depth rule: yeast Walmart stays 1.2425, ground-cumin Sam's stays 0.56, lettuce Sam's stays 1.0367, bread-crumbs Walmart stays 0.0813. That residue is real and unfixed: the newest price of a product can live in a capture too thin to be eligible, and reaching it means changing the depth rule, which do_not_touch forbids and the reviewer did not measure. See open_questions_for_brad.
(4) A WRONG PRODUCT BEHIND THE FIRST. Retiring the stale 2026-07-17 'Sweet Red Cherries, 3 lbs.' row at 2.94 exposed 'Verry Cherry Plums, 2 lbs.' at 3.43 as the Sam's cherries cell - a plum, eligible all along because cherries' only include is a bare cherr(y|ies) with no plum release. Ruled known-wrong (cherries|SamsClub|verry-cherry-plums-2-lbs) and rebuilt; the cell is now 'Sweet Red Cherries, 3 lbs.' at 3.74, which is exactly the value the plan predicted.
(5) THE REFUSAL BRANCH IS INGEST-TIME ONLY. build-walmart-deals runs at capture time, not in the board chain, so root_fix (a) has NO effect on this board: rice-cakes Walmart stays 0.467 and the plan's 0.4813 will not be observed until a new Walmart capture is built. It is scoped to WEIGHT and VOLUME units, not counts: case 8 ('Bogus Beans, 99 ct.') is a frozen fixture ruling the count path the other way, and 8f already rejects the one count shape that is unprovable. It is also scoped to SAME-FAMILY name evidence, because import-walmart-batch's frozen 'Some Sauce, 32 oz Jar' fixture (a weight name against a per-fl-oz price) caught a first cut that was too broad. The Kikkoman fish-sauce row is now refused one layer earlier, inside Build-Row, and the importer relabels it with its own documented divergence reject so the reject file and the 2026-07-27 provenance are unchanged.
(6) TWO PowerShell TRAPS COST A REBUILD EACH, both now written into the code. @() over a System.Collections.Generic.List[object] throws 'Argument types do not match' on this build (5.1.26100.9168) while .ToArray() and [object[]] work; and a List returned from a function is unrolled by the pipeline, so an empty result comes back $null and a single result comes back as a bare double, which made $strict.Count read the unroll rather than the number of readings and the refusal never fired.
